284
Durchlauchtigsten Fürst
Gnädiger Herr,
Ich glaubte gantz gewiß Ewr Durchlaucht mit heutiger Post schon etwas bestimmt — Gutes
melden zu aber der Ausbruch des Krieges behindert alles — doch wird etwas geschehen —
Trąbczyn, selbst Kaemen und Kulm erhalten Ewr durchlaucht um mehr zurück — dHerrn
Allexander hat auch sogar unserm Allgsten Herren dahin vermocht die Sache mit zu unter¬
zeichnen, daß die Pohlen die Güter die ihnen die S. Comission zurück gegeben
hat behalten sollen — folglich ist darauf keine Rechnung mehr zu machen —
Jezt reiche ich dem Kayser und Laug die gerechte Bitte ein Ewr Durchlaucht
zu dedomagiren —
Meine Berechnung soll nicht unbedeutend sein —
1. Haben Ewr Durchlaucht dem v. Broniewski seinen Pfand Schilling mit circa 60000 rt.
180 3/5 bezahlen müßen. Hierzu die 15 Jährigen Intressen 33000 rt.
Sud[?] — 93000 rt.
Hier ist zu bemerken, daß zwar Meyer Bernhard des Geld
damals gegeben, aber es steht dies Capital wie alle andere
auß Betsche und die Cujawischen Gütern eingetragen, welche
leztere den Jude M. Bernhard dafür noch jezt Pfand weg
besizt daher diese Forderung Ewr Durchlaucht allen gebührt —
2. den Kaemener Güter sind damals von Otto gerichten Taxirt 180000 rt.
Ab davon obige 60000 rt.
bleiben 120000 rt.
Es müßen demnach Ewer Durchlaucht von Kaemen erhalten 213000 rt
und zwar 93000 rt baar und für 120000 rt Gütern
3. von Trąbczyn diese Güter wäre, wie mir durch 316000 rt taxirt
darauf stehen noch die von Ewr Durchl. Contrahirten Schulden.
1. für Lichnowski 40000 rt.
2. Grotowski 20000 rt.
3. Seher Thos 8000 rt.
bleibt Werth und kommen sie durch zu Güte 246000 rt.
zusammen 459000 rt.
der Kayser oder der König muß Ewr Durchlaucht also für 366000 rt schuldenfreie
Güter geben, und jene 93000 rt müßen Sie baar erhalten —
Auf Trąbczyn ſtandern noch für Lichnowski 34000 rt. mehr, dieſe ſind aber bezahlt, indes
kan man sie nicht fordern, weil es Schulden waren die Ewr Durchl. gemacht hatten —
Weigel seine 30000 rt sind auf Zagorowo übertragen —
Die Genoreugen[?] Herrn sollen schon bleichen — und Erſt will ich nur wißen wer Ewr Durchl.
entſchädigen soll — denn werde ich ſchon was nüzt und gut ist ausſuchen —
dH. p Stägemann thut nichts man mag bitten, wie man will — jezt hat er wegen dem
Ausbruch des Krieges mehr Entschuldigungen — durch Gottes Beistand wird nun
Jedes doch etwas gelingen — Sagen kan ich noch nichts —
Pourtalès hat noch nicht geantwortet — auch die muß den Ausbruch des Krieges
ſehenen — Indes ſagt D er kommt gewiß den ſonſten hätte er abgeſchrieben. Er
war in Paris um seine Gelder einzuziehen —
dh. Napoleon soll nun wirklich bereits in Paris sein, d. den 18ten war er
nach den geſterigen Courir Nachrichten ſchon in fontainebleau. Mons Rey
ist nun auch zum Schelm geworden — Hier hat Napo[leon]: hergeschrieben,
daß man ihm seine Frau und seinen Sohn verabfolgen soll — und sie
ihm nach Paris mit ſeiner Geleit senden — O was geht doch jezt vor
Der Pöbel regiert jezt in Frankreich den diesen hat der Avanturie auf
gerufen und Freyheit und Gleicheit den Lans e[v?]itottes verheißen — Es ist
eine Nation die mann im Grunde verabſcheuen muß — die Canaille
soll dorten ärger als eine Herde Teufel Häusern und ihren Zug wo sie ziehen,
mit Grausamkeit und Gräuelthaten beschrifnen, welche kein Mensch
zu beſchreiben im Stande iſt — der König von Frankreich ſoll in Lille
sein, und was das verdauerdigste ist daß noch kein Schuß von den König
Truppen gethan — der Böse nicht zieht mit seinem Haufen dahin ungehändet
alles läuft ihm wie einen tollen Hund aus dem Wege — In dem Zeitung
sind raisonern amtes von unbegränzter Treue und Ergebenheit am König
aufgeführt, Bonapartes Macht wird bis auf 8 bis 10/m Mann herab gesezt
und gleichwohl ist der K[aiser]. in Paris und verjägt den angebeteten König —
Hier horchen die Herrn, ob mann sie nicht von Franderichs Seite um
Hülfe auffordern wird — sie Amahiren sich und laßen den Himmel wolte
Unterdes kömt der Räuber und die Canaille so weit daß man hundert
tausende zur Schlachtbank wird führen müßen — O tempora o mores — 
der K[önig]. Murat soll nun auch schon sein haupt erheben, und ehe sichs Jemand
versehen wird; hauset der in Italien, und dringt wohl bis W —
Thore — Die Noth oder die Theuerung übersteigt hier nun schon alle
Gränzen — für was soll die Armen Mobil gereicht und Krieg geführt
werden? Mann sieht die nur dencklichste Schreckens Sonnen entgegen —
die Wurtembergsche Geschichte, hat nach den diese Nacht eingegangenen Nachrichten
sich für der dicken Majestät scandaleuse gnädigte — Lesen Ewr Durchlaucht
die Beilagen und stauen Sie — der Fürst Hard: und F[ürst]. Metternich
sezzen dieses feiste Wesen auch gar arg in Grünke und nun die mehr als
unbegränzte Schande — daß seine eigene Brüder ihm so früherlich
am Pranger stellen — die armen herzog Willhelm, der doch die Rolle
des Krieges Ministers bey ihm spielte, den hat die zart danckende Majestät
ſogleich angejagt, auch den Sohn des Eugens hat er aus Allhſtern Milde
befohlen sich sogleich zum Teufel zu sehenem dem Heinrich und Loar,
hat er gedroht ewig einkerkern zu laßen — die Sache macht hier,
viel Spaß — Waß mich ärgert ist daß man die Weißheit seines
reichstags Presidenten so häßlich per[s?]itlirt. Dieser Erlauchte Herr
wird jezt sowohl hier als auch von dem Mediatisirten grausam durchgezogen.
Vieleicht bin ich im Stande mit künftiger Post trostreichere Nachrichten als bis her
einzusenden. In Ehrfurcht ersterbe
um kehren
Ewr Durchlaucht
von Teutſchen und Französische Blanquets bitte
ich sehr — ach und wäre es möglich Eberhard hier
zu sehen — den schwerlich will sich Jemand mit den Vergleich
befaßen
Wien d 27ten März
1815
 bey gehorſamſter Diener
v Triebenfeld
Nach den so eben angekommen Courir ist Bonaparte in Paris und als Kayser
bereits wieder ausgerufen — Davoust ist Krieges Minister und Seige
Minister des Innern — der Dicke fette König ſizt mit ſeine Sippſchaft nun
in Lille — Wer soll nun die fremden Truppen nach Frankreich hin rufen.
worauf die andern Herrn zu warten scheinen — O daß ist doch eine Erbärmlichkeit
ohne gleichen — Den Augenblick geht die Nachricht ein daß es in Paris
zwischen den Bonapartischen Rebellen und den Royalisten zu einer großen
Schlägerey gekommen — das Ende von diesen ist noch nicht bekannt — Ein
Glück wäre dies — den da würden die Paten wohl bald herbey gerufen werden
müßen —
In Berlin ſoll alles was geſchieht und alles was gehöhe iſt ſehr perhiſeliers
werden — der Fürst Hardenberg hat seine ganze Heiterkeit verlohren —

translation.en:
284

Most Serene Prince,

Most gracious Lord, I quite certainly believed I should be able to report something definite — something good — to Your Serene Highness by today's post, but the outbreak of the war impedes everything — yet something will come of it — Trąbczyn, and even Kamionna and Kolno, Your Serene Highness will never again recover — Mr Alexander has even induced our Most Gracious Lord to set his signature to the matter, namely that the Poles are to keep the estates which the commission restored to them — consequently no further reckoning is to be made upon that. Now I am submitting to the Emperor and the [uncertain: King] the just petition that Your Serene Highness be indemnified — my calculation shall not be an insignificant one —

1. Your Serene Highness had to pay von Broniewski his pledge-money of circa 60,000 Rthl. 180 3/5. To this the interest of 15 years, 33,000 Rthl. Total [illegible] — 93,000 Rthl.

Here it is to be observed that although Meyer Bernhard gave the money at that time, this capital nevertheless stands, like all the others, registered out of Pszczew and the Kujavian estates, the latter of which the Jew M. Bernhard still now holds in pledge for it, wherefore this claim belongs wholly to Your Serene Highness —

2. the Kamionna estates were at that time assessed by Otto's courts at 180,000 Rthl. Deduct therefrom the above 60,000 Rthl.

there remain 120,000 Rthl.

Accordingly Your Serene Highness must receive for Kamionna 213,000 Rthl, namely 93,000 Rthl in cash and 120,000 Rthl in estates

3. of Trąbczyn: these estates would be, as [assessed] by me, valued at 316,000 Rthl; upon them there still stand the debts contracted by Your Serene Highness.

1. for Lichnowski 40,000 Rthl.

2. Grotowski 20,000 Rthl.

3. Seher Thos 8,000 Rthl. there remains in value, and should they come through to the good, 246,000 Rthl, together 459,000 Rthl.

The Emperor or the King must therefore give Your Serene Highness debt-free estates to the value of 366,000 Rthl, and those 93,000 Rthl you must receive in cash — upon Trąbczyn there stood a further 34,000 Rthl for Lichnowski, but these are paid; still, one cannot demand them, because they were debts which Your Serene Highness had contracted — Weigel's 30,000 Rthl have been transferred onto Zagórów — The [illegible] gentlemen shall grow pale enough — and first I only wish to know who is to indemnify Your Serene Highness; then I shall duly pick out what is of use and good — Mr Stägemann does nothing, beg as one may — now, with the outbreak of the war, he has more excuses — with God's help something will yet succeed. I can say nothing yet — Pourtalès has still not answered — he too must be waiting to see the outbreak of the war. Meanwhile D. says he will certainly come, since otherwise he would have written off. He was in Paris to call in his monies — Napoleon is now said really to be already in Paris; on the 18th, according to yesterday's courier reports, he was already at Fontainebleau. Monsieur Rey has now also turned rogue — Napoleon has written here that his wife and his son are to be handed over to him, and sent to him at Paris under his escort — Oh, what is now afoot! The mob now rules in France, for it is the mob this adventurer has called up, promising freedom and equality to the sans-culottes — It is a nation one must at bottom abhor — the rabble there is said to be housing worse than a herd of devils, and to mark their march, wherever they go, with cruelties and atrocities which no man is able to describe — the King of France is said to be at Lille, and what is most [uncertain: lamentable] is that not a shot has yet been fired by the King's troops — the Evil One moves on with his horde unchecked; everyone gets out of his way as out of a mad dog's — In the newspapers there are reasonings [text lost] of boundless loyalty and devotion to the King

set out; Bonaparte's force is reduced to 8 to 10 thousand men, and nevertheless the Emperor is in Paris and drives out the adored King — Here the gentlemen are listening to hear whether they will not be called upon from the French side for assistance — they [uncertain: are gratifying themselves] and let it be; would to Heaven — Meanwhile the robber and the rabble get so far that hundreds of thousands will have to be led to the shambles — O tempora, o mores — King Murat too is said already to be raising his head, and before anyone is aware of it he will be housing in Italy and pressing perhaps as far as the gates of V[ienna] — The distress, or rather the dearness, here now passes all bounds — for what is the poor militia to be furnished and the war waged? One sees nothing but the most conceivable suns of terror before one — the Württemberg affair has, according to the reports come in this night, [uncertain: turned out] scandalously for the fat Majesty — Let Your Serene Highness read the enclosures and be astonished — Prince Hardenberg and Prince Metternich too set this corpulent creature very sorely in [uncertain: a corner], and now the more than boundless disgrace — that his own brothers put him so early in the pillory — the poor Duke Wilhelm, who after all played the part of Minister of War with him, him the tenderly thanking Majesty at once drove off; the son of Eugen too he has, out of his Most Gracious clemency, ordered to go straightway to the devil; Heinrich and Loar he has threatened to have imprisoned for ever — the affair affords much amusement here — What vexes me is that the wisdom of his Diet's president is so odiously [uncertain: ridiculed]. This Illustrious Lord is now being cruelly pulled to pieces, both here and by the mediatised princes. Perhaps I shall be in a position to send in more consoling news by the next post than hitherto. In deepest reverence I remain, until death,

turn over

Your Serene Highness's

Of German and French blank forms I beg most earnestly — ah, and were it possible to see Eberhard here — for hardly will anyone take the settlement in hand

Vienna, the 27th of March
1815

your most obedient servant

v Triebenfeld

According to the courier just come in, Bonaparte is in Paris and has already been proclaimed Emperor again — Davoust is Minister of War and Seige Minister of the Interior — the thick fat King now sits with his kindred at Lille — Who is now to call the foreign troops into France, which the other gentlemen appear to be waiting for — Oh, that is a wretchedness without equal — At this moment news comes in that a great brawl has broken out in Paris between the Bonapartist rebels and the Royalists — the end of it is not yet known — This would be a piece of good fortune, for then the [uncertain: godparents] would soon have to be called in — In Berlin everything that is happening and everything that is [illegible] is said to be becoming very [illegible] — Prince Hardenberg has lost all his cheerfulness —

2. the Kamionna estates were at that time assessed by Otto's courts at 180,000 Rthl. Deduct therefrom the above 60,000 Rthl.

there remain 120,000 Rthl.

Accordingly Your Serene Highness must receive for Kamionna 213,000 Rthl, namely 93,000 Rthl in cash and 120,000 Rthl in estates

3. of Trąbczyn: these estates would be, as [assessed] by me, valued at 316,000 Rthl; upon them there still stand the debts contracted by Your Serene Highness.

1. for Lichnowski 40,000 Rthl.

2. Grotowski 20,000 Rthl.

3. Seher Thos 8,000 Rthl. there remains in value, and should they come through to the good, 246,000 Rthl, together 459,000 Rthl.

The Emperor or the King must therefore give Your Serene Highness debt-free estates to the value of 366,000 Rthl, and those 93,000 Rthl you must receive in cash — upon Trąbczyn there stood a further 34,000 Rthl for Lichnowski, but these are paid; still, one cannot demand them, because they were debts which Your Serene Highness had contracted — Weigel's 30,000 Rthl have been transferred onto Zagórów — The [illegible] gentlemen shall grow pale enough — and first I only wish to know who is to indemnify Your Serene Highness; then I shall duly pick out what is of use and good — Mr Stägemann does nothing, beg as one may — now, with the outbreak of the war, he has more excuses — with God's help something will yet succeed. I can say nothing yet — Pourtalès has still not answered — he too must be waiting to see the outbreak of the war. Meanwhile D. says he will certainly come, since otherwise he would have written off. He was in Paris to call in his monies — Napoleon is now said really to be already in Paris; on the 18th, according to yesterday's courier reports, he was already at Fontainebleau. Monsieur Rey has now also turned rogue — Napoleon has written here that his wife and his son are to be handed over to him, and sent to him at Paris under his escort — Oh, what is now afoot! The mob now rules in France, for it is the mob this adventurer has called up, promising freedom and equality to the sans-culottes — It is a nation one must at bottom abhor — the rabble there is said to be housing worse than a herd of devils, and to mark their march, wherever they go, with cruelties and atrocities which no man is able to describe — the King of France is said to be at Lille, and what is most [uncertain: lamentable] is that not a shot has yet been fired by the King's troops — the Evil One moves on with his horde unchecked; everyone gets out of his way as out of a mad dog's — In the newspapers there are reasonings [text lost] of boundless loyalty and devotion to the King

set out; Bonaparte's force is reduced to 8 to 10 thousand men, and nevertheless the Emperor is in Paris and drives out the adored King — Here the gentlemen are listening to hear whether they will not be called upon from the French side for assistance — they [uncertain: are gratifying themselves] and let it be; would to Heaven — Meanwhile the robber and the rabble get so far that hundreds of thousands will have to be led to the shambles — O tempora, o mores — King Murat too is said already to be raising his head, and before anyone is aware of it he will be housing in Italy and pressing perhaps as far as the gates of V[ienna] — The distress, or rather the dearness, here now passes all bounds — for what is the poor militia to be furnished and the war waged? One sees nothing but the most conceivable suns of terror before one — the Württemberg affair has, according to the reports come in this night, [uncertain: turned out] scandalously for the fat Majesty — Let Your Serene Highness read the enclosures and be astonished — Prince Hardenberg and Prince Metternich too set this corpulent creature very sorely in [uncertain: a corner], and now the more than boundless disgrace — that his own brothers put him so early in the pillory — the poor Duke Wilhelm, who after all played the part of Minister of War with him, him the tenderly thanking Majesty at once drove off; the son of Eugen too he has, out of his Most Gracious clemency, ordered to go straightway to the devil; Heinrich and Loar he has threatened to have imprisoned for ever — the affair affords much amusement here — What vexes me is that the wisdom of his Diet's president is so odiously [uncertain: ridiculed]. This Illustrious Lord is now being cruelly pulled to pieces, both here and by the mediatised princes. Perhaps I shall be in a position to send in more consoling news by the next post than hitherto. In deepest reverence I remain, until death,

turn over

Your Serene Highness's

Of German and French blank forms I beg most earnestly — ah, and were it possible to see Eberhard here — for hardly will anyone take the settlement in hand

Vienna, the 27th of March
1815

your most obedient servant

v Triebenfeld

According to the courier just come in, Bonaparte is in Paris and has already been proclaimed Emperor again — Davoust is Minister of War and Seige Minister of the Interior — the thick fat King now sits with his kindred at Lille — Who is now to call the foreign troops into France, which the other gentlemen appear to be waiting for — Oh, that is a wretchedness without equal — At this moment news comes in that a great brawl has broken out in Paris between the Bonapartist rebels and the Royalists — the end of it is not yet known — This would be a piece of good fortune, for then the [uncertain: godparents] would soon have to be called in — In Berlin everything that is happening and everything that is [illegible] is said to be becoming very [illegible] — Prince Hardenberg has lost all his cheerfulness —
summary_en: Triebenfeld reports that Trąbczyn, Kamionna and Kolno are no longer to be expected: he says Alexander has secured that the Poles keep the estates returned to them. He applies for compensation. For Kamionna he demands 93,000 Rthl in cash (the Broniewski mortgage sum together with interest) and 120,000 Rthl in estates. For Trąbczyn, valued at 316,000 Rthl, 246,000 Rthl remain after deduction of the debts. In all 459,000 Rthl. Weigel's 30,000 Rthl have been transferred to Zagórów. Stägemann does nothing. He asks for blank forms and for Eberhard to come because of the settlement.
summary_de: Triebenfeld meldet, dass Trąbczyn, Kamionna und Kolno nicht mehr zu erwarten sind: Alexander habe erreicht, dass die Polen die ihnen zurückgegebenen Güter behalten. Er beantragt Entschädigung. Für Kamionna fordert er 93000 Rthl baar (Pfandschilling Broniewski samt Zinsen) und 120000 Rthl in Gütern. Für Trąbczyn, taxiert auf 316000 Rthl, bleiben nach Abzug der Schulden 246000 Rthl. Insgesamt 459000 Rthl. Weigels 30000 Rthl sind auf Zagórów übertragen. Stägemann tut nichts. Bittet um Blanquets und um Eberhards Kommen wegen des Vergleichs.

reading.notes: Triebenfeld writes from Vienna to the Prince. The outbreak of war is holding everything up. Trąbczyn, Kamionna and Kolno will not come back to the Prince: Alexander got "unsern Allgsten Herren" to sign that the Poles keep the estates the commission returned to them. Triebenfeld is therefore petitioning for compensation and sets out his calculation. Kamionna: 93000 rt in cash plus 120000 rt in estates. Trąbczyn: valued at 316000 rt, net 246000 rt after debts. Total 459000 rt: 366000 rt in debt-free estates plus 93000 rt in cash. Weigel's 30000 rt have been moved onto Zagorowo. Stägemann is doing nothing and Pourtalès has not answered. The rest is news of Napoleon, Paris, Murat and Württemberg. He asks for blank forms and wants Eberhard in Vienna for the settlement.
